prompts.text:
You are drafting one section of a consultation note as prose.

Task:
Write the section named below, using only the consult draft and the author's notes for this section.

Guardrail:
Do not add clinical facts the draft does not contain. Where the draft is silent, say so plainly.

Output rule:
Return only prose for this section. No heading, no bullets, no table, no commentary.

Section:
History

Author's notes for this section:
Falls and the postural drop.

Consult draft:
Ana Souza, 72, seen for falls. Two falls in a month; postural drop 24 mmHg. On doxazosin, ramipril and bendroflumethiazide. Doxazosin stopped today; review in three weeks; return sooner if she faints. New patient, 40 minutes. (Fictional.)

You are drafting one section of a consultation note as a table.

Task:
Lay the section named below out as one markdown table, using only the consult draft and the author's notes for this section. Choose the columns the section calls for (for a medication list: name, dose, frequency, indication).

Guardrail:
Do not add clinical facts the draft does not contain. Leave a cell blank rather than inferring it.

Output rule:
Return only the markdown table, with a header row. No heading above it, no prose, no commentary.

Section:
Medications

Author's notes for this section:
Include the doxazosin stopped today.

Consult draft:
Ana Souza, 72, seen for falls. Two falls in a month; postural drop 24 mmHg. On doxazosin, ramipril and bendroflumethiazide. Doxazosin stopped today; review in three weeks; return sooner if she faints. New patient, 40 minutes. (Fictional.)

You are closing a consultation note with one line about what it leaves out.

The sections the author asked for, and whether each was produced:

- History: produced

- Medications: produced

- Social history: left out at the author's request


Output rule:
Return one sentence naming the sections left out at the author's request, or, if none were, one sentence saying every requested section was produced. No heading, no list, no commentary.

You are writing one sentence for the patient about one section of their consultation.

Task:
In plain language a patient can read, write one sentence that says what the section named below covers, drawing only on the consult draft and the author's notes.

Guardrail:
No clinical jargon, no facts the draft does not contain, no advice.

Output rule:
Return exactly one sentence. No heading, no list, no commentary.

Section:
History

Author's notes for this section:
Falls and the postural drop.

Consult draft:
Ana Souza, 72, seen for falls. Two falls in a month; postural drop 24 mmHg. On doxazosin, ramipril and bendroflumethiazide. Doxazosin stopped today; review in three weeks; return sooner if she faints. New patient, 40 minutes. (Fictional.)

You are tailoring a standing section of a consultation note to this consult.

Task:
Write the section named below by following its standard against the consult draft.

Guardrail:
Do not add clinical facts the draft does not contain. Where the standard asks for something the draft does not document, say that it is not documented.

Output rule:
Return only prose for this section. No heading, no bullets, no commentary.

Section:
Safety netting

Section standard:
One short paragraph telling the patient and the referrer what should prompt an earlier review: the symptoms or changes the draft names as warning signs, and who to contact. Draw only on what the draft documents; where it names no warning signs, say that none were documented.


Consult draft:
Ana Souza, 72, seen for falls. Two falls in a month; postural drop 24 mmHg. On doxazosin, ramipril and bendroflumethiazide. Doxazosin stopped today; review in three weeks; return sooner if she faints. New patient, 40 minutes. (Fictional.)

Section:
Follow-up

Section standard:
One short paragraph stating when and how the patient will be seen again, and what will be reviewed then, as the draft documents it. Where the draft sets no follow-up, say that none was arranged.
